solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Escort to the ground for clash

parts.note: to escort someone is to show them (in, out or round)
going to the ground is going down

explanation.surface: A guide takes someone down to the pitch before a fight breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive final confrontation is a clash between rivals.

clue.text: Phone engineer around noon

indicators.note: the word for engineer is placed around the letter for noon

parts.note: to engineer something is to rig it, fix it dishonestly

explanation.surface: Someone calls a repair engineer at about midday.
explanation.definitionFit: To phone someone is to ring them, a common British idiom for calling.

clue.text: TV series — it's funny, endless tease

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of it's, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: endless means the word for tease loses its last letter

parts.note: to tease hair is to comb it out

explanation.surface: A television show is described as amusing, with a never-ending tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a type of TV series, usually shortened to this word.

clue.text: Money to get sheer wool

parts.note: cash is money
sheer, as in sheer luck, means mere or utter

explanation.surface: Spending money to buy fine fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine soft wool from Kashmir goats is known by this name.

clue.text: Promising? Doubtful, with a change of leadership

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader of the word, is swapped for the letter A from the clue's own 'a'

parts.note: doubtful means suspicious, distrusting

explanation.surface: Is something promising, or doubtful once the people in charge change?
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a change of leadership' replaces the S at the head of SUSPICIOUS with A.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspicious start is a promising one, full of good omens.

clue.text: Suspension of business in bay

definitions.meaning: a break when Parliament or a court stops sitting
an alcove or niche set back in a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary break and an alcove in a wall share this one word.

clue.text: Novel story of an orphan girl breaking finger

indicators.note: the orphan girl breaks into the word for finger, sitting inside it

parts.note: a finger of whisky is a small measure, a tot
Heidi is the orphan girl of Johanna Spyri's children's novel

explanation.surface: A book tells of an orphaned girl who breaks her finger.
explanation.walkthrough: A finger is a measure of spirits, as is a tot.
explanation.definitionFit: Dostoevsky's novel about Prince Myshkin bears this title.

clue.text: Telephone number to secure file, a hand-held tool

indicators.note: the abbreviation holds the file securely within it

parts.note: Tel. is the abbreviation printed before a telephone number
a file of people is a row or line

explanation.surface: A phone number is needed to secure a file, which is apparently a tool you hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bladed implement used by gardeners and bricklayers, held in one hand.

clue.text: Astuteness shown by a copper confronting workers

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A police officer shows shrewdness when facing a group of labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewdness and keen insight are what this word for business sharpness denotes.

clue.text: Suddenly see toupee on teacher's head

indicators.note: the toupee sits on the head, so in this across answer it is placed after the teacher's letter
the head of the word teacher is its first letter

parts.note: a toupee is a hairpiece, a wig

explanation.surface: A pupil spots a hairpiece on the teacher's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to twig is to grasp or realise all at once.

clue.text: Helicopter carrying foolish old peasant

indicators.note: the helicopter word carries the jumbled letters inside it

parts.note: chopper is slang for a helicopter

indicators.note: foolish means silly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A helicopter gives a lift to a silly old farm labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy rustic, a heavy-footed farm labourer, is a pejorative name for a peasant.

clue.text: Record crowd, an immovable mass

parts.note: a log is a record, as a ship's log
a jam is a crush or crowd

explanation.surface: A record crowd forms a solid block of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle of floating timber that blocks a river, hence any immovable mass or deadlock.

clue.text: US novelist and sailor needing capital

parts.note: Jack, or Jack tar, is a sailor
London is the UK capital

explanation.surface: An American writer and a seaman need money.
explanation.definitionFit: The American author of The Call of the Wild.

clue.text: Use train

definitions.meaning: to employ or exert, as in using a right
to drill or work out the body

explanation.definitionFit: Exerting a right and drilling the body are both expressed by this verb.

clue.text: Steal the Spanish coin

parts.note: nick is British slang for steal
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone pockets a coin from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A US five-cent coin is so called after the metal.

clue.text: Mine included in these silly nicknames, maybe

indicators.note: the mine word is included inside the scrambled letters
silly means daft, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Silly nicknames are given to a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive bynames such as the Great are epithets, of which nicknames are one example.

clue.text: Girl carrying on in Italian city

indicators.note: the girl's name carries the little word within it

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl goes on living in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in the Veneto where Romeo and Juliet is set.

clue.text: A way into flying with the aircraft industry

parts.note: via means by way of

indicators.note: flying means scattering in all directions, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A path into flight is offered by working in aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The design, building and operation of aircraft is the industry this word names.

clue.text: Organised tour inside walls of sacred place in Gloucestershire

indicators.note: the jumbled tour sits inside the outer letters
the walls of a word are its outside letters
organised means arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guided tour goes on within the walls of a church in the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloucestershire is a county in the west of England, so 'place' is the definition and 'sacred' only gives its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in the Cotswolds of Gloucestershire.

clue.text: Complete list as quickly as possible

parts.note: full means complete
to list is to lean, to tilt

explanation.surface: A complete list is wanted urgently.
explanation.definitionFit: Running at full tilt means going at top speed, from jousting.

clue.text: Loud outcry at college over poisoned arrow wife fired

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford

indicators.note: poisoned means corrupted, so the letters are scrambled
fired means let go, so the wife's letter is removed

explanation.surface: Uproar on campus as a poisoned arrow is shot at a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wife fired' takes W from ARROW, leaving ARRO, and 'poisoned' turns that into ROAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy public protest or tumult is a loud outcry.

clue.text: Let oneself down causing trouble over mad cow disease

indicators.note: the trouble word is spread over the disease, enclosing it

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease

explanation.surface: Something is causing trouble over the cattle disease.
explanation.definitionFit: To descend a rock face by rope is to lower oneself down, here punning on disappointing oneself.

clue.text: Grant, a fine US president

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
Gerald Ford was a US president

explanation.surface: Grant was a fine American president.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses Grant was also a US president, so 'Grant' looks like a name, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant or allow someone something is to afford it to them.

clue.text: Pain?

parts.note: pain is the French word for bread, so the clue asks for a long loaf from France

explanation.surface: A single word asks about suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin baguette is the bread the French call pain.

clue.text: Model with the ultimate in elegance on location

parts.note: to model for an artist is to sit

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A model brings the height of elegance to a shoot on location.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or location.

clue.text: Rifle fire

definitions.meaning: to plunder or ransack a place
to dismiss someone from a job

explanation.definitionFit: Plundering a town and dismissing a worker are both this one verb.

clue.text: Dish featured in red-top abroad

parts.note: a red-top is a British tabloid, informally a rag
abroad means out and about

explanation.surface: A meal is reported in a tabloid newspaper overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: A red-top is a British tabloid newspaper, named for its red masthead.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly seasoned stew of meat and vegetables, a French dish.

clue.text: Dreadful, film star missing entrance — he won't be pleased

parts.note: dire means dreadful

indicators.note: missing its entrance means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a film star is an actor

explanation.surface: A dreadful film star misses an entrance and the boss will not be happy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: the person running the film is the one displeased by a missed entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A film's director is the person displeased when an actor misses a cue.
